mara.activity: Wake slowly, drink water, and check in with how I feel before getting up.
mara.intention: Start gently and notice whether I am well enough for the day.

mara.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, and change into workout clothes.
Do a short, deliberately moderate strength workout and shower afterward.
mara.intention: Keep my usual routine while respecting that I am still recovering.

mara.activity: Dress for work, have a quick breakfast, and leave for the studio.
mara.intention: Eat enough to support the long day without making a production of it.

mara.activity: Work at the studio on planting plans, coordination, and site-visit follow-up.
mara.intention: Keep the day structured and make steady progress before the evening class.

mara.activity: Eat a simple lunch and take a short quiet break.
mara.intention: Protect enough energy for the rest of the day.

mara.activity: Continue studio work, meetings, and site-related coordination.
mara.intention: Finish the workday cleanly rather than carrying every loose end into the evening.

mara.activity: Make the call to my parent or older relative about the health, appointment, or future-arrangement concern, listening carefully and taking notes.
mara.intention: Sound calm while understanding what practical responsibility may be needed next.

mara.activity: Travel to the ceramics class and have a small snack if needed.
mara.intention: Shift out of work mode before class.

mara.activity: Attend the second ceramics class and work slowly through the exercises, allowing the pieces to be imperfect.
mara.intention: Enjoy being a beginner and let concentration exist without a client-ready result.

mara.activity: Return home, change into comfortable clothes, and put my keys deliberately in the entryway while removing my shoes.
mara.intention: Arrive without bringing the whole day into the rooms.

mara.activity: Make a simple dinner for myself at the kitchen island: scrambled eggs and toast, then carry it to the living room.
mara.intention: Eat something warm and manageable instead of ordering or trying to host.

mara.activity: Eat quietly in the living room and let the ceramics class settle in my mind.
mara.intention: Have a small, restorative end to a demanding day while Julian is at dinner service.

mara.activity: Carry the plate, fork, and mug to the kitchen, rinse them, and straighten only the immediate counter space.
mara.intention: Leave the kitchen calm without turning tidying into another task.

mara.activity: Wash up, brush my teeth, and change into sleep clothes.
mara.intention: Wind down and support another full recovery night.

mara.activity: Read a few pages in bed if I can stay awake comfortably, then place my reading glasses on my nightstand and set my phone beside them.
mara.intention: Close the day quietly rather than revisiting the family call or work messages.
Give my body a full night to recover.

julian.activity: Wake beside Mara, wash up, and make quiet coffee and a small breakfast at the kitchen island. I grind the coffee beans, pour milk into a mug, eat a banana, and skim the restaurant notebook without starting major planning.
julian.intention: Ease into the morning with a familiar routine and avoid adding pressure before work.

julian.activity: Rinse the mug and breakfast things, wipe the island, and fill my thermos. I check my phone and wallet, send Mara a short reassuring message without pressing her to explain anything, then take my keys from the piano’s middle shelf.
julian.intention: Leave the house prepared while offering Mara quiet support.

julian.activity: Pack my backpack, put on my work clothes and kitchen clogs, and travel to the restaurant.
julian.intention: Arrive with enough time to settle in before Friday prep begins.

julian.activity: Handle restaurant prep, deliveries, and kitchen management. I check produce and temperatures, organize the prep list, speak with the manager, portion ingredients, and keep an eye on the Friday service setup.
julian.intention: Get the kitchen orderly before the crowded evening and prevent small problems from becoming service problems.

julian.activity: Take a short staff meal and reset in the kitchen, drinking from my thermos and reviewing the evening notes. I make a few practical adjustments to the prep list rather than starting new menu experiments.
julian.intention: Refuel and preserve energy for the long dinner service.

julian.activity: Change into a fresh work shirt, check the final service notes, tuck any receipts into the restaurant notebook, and prepare the kitchen for the evening rush.
julian.intention: Move from prep mode into service mode with the essentials accounted for.

julian.activity: Work dinner service and closing duties. I coordinate the line, taste sauces, manage tickets, finish the last cleanup, and lock up after the rush has fully cleared.
julian.intention: Keep the service calm and generous despite the Friday crowd, then close thoroughly.

julian.activity: Travel home, carry the thermos to the kitchen beside the sink, put my keys on the piano’s middle shelf, and leave my wallet and earplugs on the living room coffee table. I wash my hands and change out of my jacket.
julian.intention: Complete the familiar transition home without making extra decisions.

julian.activity: Take a hot shower, dry off, and change into sleep clothes. I keep the lights low and leave the towel hanging in the bathroom.
julian.intention: Let the heat take the edge off the service and settle my body for sleep.

julian.activity: Eat a small bowl of yogurt and drink water, rinse the bowl and glass, plug my phone into the bedroom charger, and get into bed beside Mara without turning on the television.
julian.intention: Have something gentle before bed and end the demanding day quietly.
